h1: The 5 Best Small Safes for Money of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Small Safes for Money: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five small cash safes from Bonsaii, Voncabay, Yuanshikj and others, compared by access method, mounting and budget.
summary: The Bonsaii 0.23 Cu.Ft safe is our pick for most cash storage because it has a USB-C backup if the battery dies. Voncabay adds a wrong-code lockout, the money safe with two codes suits shared access, Bonsaii 0.6 holds more, and Yuanshikj is the cheapest.
intro: A cash safe that locks you out is worse than none. The most overlooked spec is not steel thickness, it is what happens when the keypad battery dies at the wrong moment.

We reviewed five small safes and ranked them on access methods, mounting, capacity and price bucket. Facts for each come from listing details, and none of these claim a fire or burglary rating, so treat them as everyday cash and valuables storage.

products.name: Bonsaii Small Safe Box with Electronic Keypad for Valuables, 0.23 Cu.Ft
products.verdict: USB-C emergency power means a dead battery will not lock you out.
products.description:
The Bonsaii 0.23 Cu.Ft safe is a mountable steel box with pre-drilled installation holes and a USB-C emergency power backup, in the $25-50 bucket.

It leads the group because the dead-battery fallback addresses the biggest practical risk of any keypad safe. The Voncabay beside it wins on lockout features instead.

Good for household cash you must always reach. Capacity is small at 0.23 cu ft.
products.idealFor: Households that cannot risk a dead-battery lockout.
products.skipIf: You need more than a shoebox of space.

products.name: Voncabay Money Safe Box for Home with Digital Keypad, 0.23 Cu. Ft., Black
products.verdict: Three wrong codes trigger a five-minute lockout.
products.description:
The Voncabay is a 0.23 cu ft mountable steel box with a 3-wrong-entry, 5-minute lockout and a bundled fireproof and waterproof document bag, in the $25-50 bucket.

Second place is because it relies on the keypad alone, without the USB-C fallback that puts the Bonsaii first. The lockout deters code guessing.

Buy it if guessing is your worry. The bag is a bonus, not a rated safe.
products.skipIf: You want an emergency power port.

products.name: Digital Electronic Money Safe, Steel Security Lock Box with Keypad, Office
products.verdict: Two independent access codes for shared cash.
products.description:
This 4.6 liter steel box uses SPCC steel, has a mountable design, supports two independent access codes and ships with a carpet liner and manual, in the $25-50 bucket.

It ranks third since the two-code feature is useful only to shared users, while the Bonsaii offers a more broadly useful backup. It is about the same price.

Good for a small office or two-person household. Check for an emergency access option yourself.

products.name: Bonsaii Safe Box with Electronic Keypad for Home Office, 0.6 Cu.Ft
products.verdict: The roomiest safe here, with two 18mm bolts and a removable shelf.
products.description:
The Bonsaii 0.6 Cu.Ft safe has a removable shelf, two 18mm steel locking bolts, and code, key or USB-C emergency access, in the $50-100 bucket.

Fourth place is purely a price and size matter: it costs a bucket more than the small safes but gives over twice their space. It matches the smaller Bonsaii on backup power.

Buy it for larger cash volumes. For a few bills, it is overkill.
products.skipIf: You only store a little cash.

products.name: Yuanshikj Small Steel Security Safe Box with Keypad, Key, 0.23 CuFt, Black
products.verdict: The cheapest anchored safe, with dual steel bolts.
products.description:
The Yuanshikj is a 0.2 cu ft mountable steel box with dual steel locking bolts, a magnetic auto-lock door and included mounting hardware, in the under $25 bucket.

It sits last only because the Bonsaii models add USB-C backup that it lacks. In exchange it costs the least of any mounted safe here.

Buy it for a first, low-cost cash box. Keep a key somewhere safe, but not inside it.
products.idealFor: First-time buyers on a tight budget.

whatMatters.detail: A keypad safe runs on batteries, so a USB-C port or a backup key matters. Without one a dead battery locks you out. Look for the words emergency power or override key in the listing.
A safe you can bolt down is much harder to carry off. It matters because small safes are easy to steal. Check that pre-drilled holes and screws are included.
Bolts hold the door shut. It matters because thicker bolts resist prying. Look for bolt diameter, like the 18mm bolts on the larger Bonsaii.
A wrong-entry lockout slows code guessing. It matters if others have access to your space. Look for a stated number of tries and delay.
Capacity is interior volume in cubic feet. It matters because stacks of cash and papers fill small safes quickly. Compare interior dimensions, not only the exterior.

faq.a: None of these list a fire rating. The Voncabay's bundled bag is described as fireproof and waterproof, but it is a bag, not the safe.
Leaving the safe unmounted. A small box can simply be carried away.

faq.q: Is the larger Bonsaii worth it?
faq.a: Only if you need the space. For small amounts the 0.23 version works.
Several include pre-drilled holes and hardware, so use them to anchor it.
Keypads need batteries. The Bonsaii models offer USB-C backup power.

faq.q: Can I keep the key inside?
faq.a: No. Keep spare keys outside the safe.

finalTake: The Bonsaii Small Safe Box 0.23 Cu.Ft is the best-balanced buy thanks to its USB-C backup. Choose the Voncabay for lockout protection, the 0.6 Bonsaii for space, and the Yuanshikj when budget matters most.
